audience.programmeDescription: Utrecht’s Computer Science bachelor studies how computer systems work and how to design and test software. This example shows the general Dutch-taught degree and its required team software project.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The UCR option combines programming, databases, operating systems, algorithms and mathematical foundations with data and AI. Utrecht also offers a 15 EC individual thesis within its profiling space, alongside the required team project.

cellNotes.text: Both develop imperative programming and problem solving. UCR uses Python.
Both cover computer networks. UCR also examines operating systems, while Utrecht gives dedicated attention to computer architecture.
Both develop formal logic for computer science. UCR also covers discrete mathematics and proof.
Both study relational databases. UCR includes SQL, normalisation and query processing.
Both study data structures and algorithms for organising and searching data.
UCR’s Software Development course introduces functional programming in Haskell. Utrecht gives the subject a separate required course.
UCR’s Networks & Operating Systems course introduces processes, threads and concurrency. Utrecht gives concurrency a separate advanced course.
UCR studies image processing and recognition. Utrecht’s graphics course focuses on generating images with computer graphics.
Both develop software construction and testing. UCR combines C++ and Haskell with version control and code review.

Both develop statistical tools for research. Utrecht also teaches computer-science research design, literature review and reporting. Utrecht recommends taking this course in period 1 of Year 3 if the Software Project follows in periods 3 and 4.
Utrecht applies introductory computing in a dedicated project. UCR’s product design course contributes related prototyping practice.
Both develop methods for intelligent systems. UCR focuses on decisions and reasoning under uncertainty.
Utrecht offers IT law as a major elective. UCR’s AI Ethics addresses privacy, fairness and accountability from an ethical perspective.
Utrecht offers a dedicated Web Technology elective.
Both develop advanced algorithm design and analysis.
Both develop data analysis. Utrecht also covers information retrieval.

Utrecht requires a 15 EC team software project for a client. UCR’s optional independent research is separate from the scheduled courses. Utrecht invites eligible students to register. Teams develop software for a client over two teaching periods.
Choose 45 EC, including at least 15 EC at intermediate or advanced level. An optional individual thesis can count here.

notes.text: Utrecht requires separate courses in computer architecture, functional programming and concurrency, and a 15 EC team project. UCR covers parts of those subjects within broader systems and software courses. IT law and Web Technology are examples of Utrecht’s restricted electives.

ACCPPDE101.name: Personal & Professional Development
ACCPPDE101.text: This course is a first-year requirement and aims to stimulate personal development, namely, being able to actively, consciously and ethically orientate oneself in relation to others and the world. It supports the development of core personal and academic skills that enhance critical thinking and independent learning. It seeks to improve and develop academic writing and presenting skills and helps students develop the foundational skills and attitudes to reflect on societal issues and engage with societal partners.

BENENTR111.name: Consumer Product Design
BENENTR111.text: You will learn how to function in a ‘real-world’ design and development team for consumer products. We go through the phases of design and development: probe customer needs, translate these into a product concept, develop a fabrication method, analyze sustainability, analyze costs and proceeds. Design and development involves interviewing customers, brainstorming, laboratory experiments, quantitative modeling, constructing a prototype, and considering protection of intellectual property.

source.reviewNote: CP089: reviewed the unchanged official description against current course content. The existing text supports the stated scope.

DISARIN111.name: AI Ethics
DISARIN111.text: AI Ethics examines artificial intelligence from philosophical and psychological perspectives. Topics include fairness, privacy, responsibility, human-value alignment, moral status and political or existential risks. Students apply ethical frameworks to questions about human behaviour and interaction, synthesise research in an analytical psychology project, and produce a research-based podcast.

DISARIN211.name: Decision-making in AI
DISARIN211.text: Decision-making in AI examines how intelligent agents make decisions under uncertainty. Students study probability, Bayesian networks, temporal models, expected utility, Markov decision processes, partial observability and bandit problems. Multi-agent decisions and probabilistic programming extend the analysis, supported by equations, numerical examples and scientific papers.

DISARIN212.name: Logic & Discrete Mathematics
DISARIN212.text: Introduces formal logic, abstract reasoning and proof. Students work with propositions, quantified statements, sets, Boolean algebra, functions and relations, direct and indirect proofs, induction and recursion. A final component models processes and games without chance and investigates winning strategies.

DISARIN311.name: Optimization Methods in AI
DISARIN311.text: Optimization Methods in AI studies search and optimisation for rational agents. Topics include uninformed and heuristic search, local and global optimisation, adversarial search, constraint satisfaction, linear programming and discrete optimisation. Laboratory exercises and projects develop algorithm implementation, evaluation and experimental investigation of small intelligent systems.

DISDATA212.text: Image Processing & Computer Vision studies how digital images are represented, processed and interpreted to recognise structures and objects. Topics include colour, image statistics, filtering, segmentation, feature detection, tracking and object classification. Practical work uses Python and OpenCV to develop and benchmark an image-recognition pipeline on previously unseen images.

Students build and train networks, study backpropagation, regularisation and model evaluation, and apply deep learning to computer vision, time series and text, including transformers. Projects investigate prediction problems and report experimental results.

GOSPHIL212.name: Ethics
GOSPHIL212.text: Ethics examines moral reasoning through historical and contemporary theories and close philosophical reading. Students study utilitarianism, Kantian ethics, virtue ethics, contractarianism and feminist ethics, alongside Nietzsche, Murdoch and Nagel. Reflection and research essays develop interpretation, argument evaluation and an independent position on ethical theory or a practical ethical problem.

MCCCOMM111.text: The Art of Rhetorical Communication develops rhetorical analysis, academic writing and oral presentation. Students examine classical Western roots and the canons of rhetoric, and learn to construct, organise and support persuasive arguments. Historical and contemporary examples connect rhetorical theory with practical communication.
